input: Call the insurance company about the roof claim

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is opening a new claim, following up on an existing one, or disputing a decision changes what the user needs to prepare and say.
Understanding what caused the roof damage (storm, leak, fallen tree, age) determines the right language to use and what documentation is relevant.
Knowing if there is a specific adjuster, claim number, or department to ask for affects how to route the call efficiently.
A deadline (e.g., claim filing window, scheduled inspection, contractor waiting) changes how urgently this call needs to happen.
Knowing what documents or information the user has on hand (policy number, photos, estimates) determines what they need to gather before calling.
The desired outcome — approval, a scheduled inspection, a payout amount, or just an update — shapes what the user should ask for and how to close the call.
If the user has had prior difficult interactions or wants to take notes, escalate, or record the call, the plan should reflect that communication strategy.

gold.taskTitle: Call insurance company about roof claim
gold.taskDescription: The user needs to make a phone call to their insurance company to handle a roof-related insurance claim.

questions.title: Is this a new claim or an existing follow-up?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is filing a roof claim for the first time or following up on a claim already in progress.

questions.title: What caused the roof damage?
questions.description: Identify the event or condition that damaged the roof (e.g., storm, hail, fallen tree, slow leak) so the right claim category and terminology can be used.

questions.title: Do you have a claim number or adjuster contact?
questions.description: Find out if the user already has a claim number, a named adjuster, or a specific department to reach, which determines how to route the call.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or time pressure on this?
questions.description: Check whether there is a filing window, scheduled inspection, contractor start date, or other deadline making this call urgent.

questions.title: What documents or info do you have ready?
questions.description: Assess what the user currently has available — policy number, damage photos, contractor estimates — to identify any gaps before calling.

questions.title: What specific outcome do you need from this call?
questions.description: Clarify the desired result — a claim approval, inspection scheduling, payout update, or coverage question answered — to keep the call focused.

questions.title: Have you had trouble with this insurer before?
questions.description: Understand if the user has faced pushback, delays, or disputes with this company, which would affect tone, escalation strategy, and note-taking approach.
